title: Light Speed Stop 10: Proxima b, Life?
topic: Light-speed journey stop 10: Proxima Centauri b (4.2 light-years; ~11-day year; habitable zone; red dwarf flares; probably tidally locked; atmosphere unknown)
links_to_previous: Answers episode 9's cliffhanger (could the planet at our nearest star hold life?): maybe, nobody knows yet. The journey continues out to the wider galaxy.
cliffhanger_question: Are there more planets than stars in our galaxy? Yes or no?
summary: Answer: maybe. Proxima b orbits in its star's habitable zone, 4.2 light-years away, but flares and tidal locking may strip its air. We still don't know if it has an atmosphere. Next stop: the Milky Way.

scenes.narration: Proxima b sits in its star's habitable zone, where water could stay liquid.

visual.query: Proxima Centauri b exoplanet artist concept

scenes.narration: It's about the size of Earth, and it's only four light-years away.
But its year lasts just eleven days.

visual.query: exoplanet orbit red dwarf artist concept

scenes.narration: Its star is a red dwarf, and red dwarfs throw violent flares.
One flare could blast the planet with radiation, and strip away its air.
It's also probably tidally locked, one side always facing its star.
So one side may burn, while the other freezes.

visual.query: exoplanet day night side artist concept

scenes.narration: The thin ring between them might be mild enough for life.
We can't see its atmosphere yet. Scientists think telescopes may soon.
But our galaxy holds hundreds of billions of stars.
Next stop, the Milky Way. Are there more planets than stars? Yes or no?
